name: Iran nuclear programme
value: No IAEA access; US strike threat 26 Nov
summary: Trump says on 26 Nov the US would hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain site if strikes resume; IAEA still lacks access
state: President Trump told reporters on 26 Nov that if the US took action it would hit Pickaxe Mountain, a fortified underground site near Natanz, but that no real activity had been seen there (Business Standard). The IAEA said on 13 Nov it could not verify the size or location of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile (The National). Credible strike threats and curtailed access keep Watch; no strike on a nuclear site, NPT withdrawal or weaponisation evidence found.
for_you: Escalation over Iran's nuclear programme could disrupt Gulf energy and travel. Travellers should follow FCDO travel advice for Iran and the region.
rubric_hit: Inspector access curtailed and credible strike threats = Watch

sources.title: Business Standard — US could hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site if strikes resume: Trump
The National — IAEA expresses concern over Iranian underground uranium-enrichment plant

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
